lines.en: : And remember, Hima-chan — no talking about the Cold War around Uncle Geoffrey. He’s at an age now where we can’t be riling him up like that.
: Yes, Mom. Though, I’m not quite sure what sort of girl you see me as if this is something you need to warn me about first thing in the morning.
: I’m only doing it now because I know your father won’t and because some of us have jobs that we need to go to today.
: All you do is tell people to stay away from sugar while I am expected to nurture the mind of someone smarter than me. It’s like high school all over again.
: I’m pretty sure that’s the point, Dad. I guess at least now you get to do it from the comfort of your own home, though.
: I’m pretty sure Ayane could do her job from home too if she wasn’t so focused on being the best nutritionist she can be.
: Like, what do you do that couldn’t be handled over a Zoom call? Why do you need to go to an office?
: Maybe she’s having an affair.
: Are you having an affair, Ayane? Is it because I’m not sad anymore?
: Oh, Akira. Sadness is so ingrained into your personality that you still exude it even when everything is going perfectly.
: The reason I’m having an affair is because you’re boring.
: She makes a good point, Dad. I don’t think there’s much you can do about that this late into life either. I think you’ve just gotta let her go.
: Oh well. It’s been a good run. See you in court for the custody battle, I guess.
: Do either of you want pancakes? I figured I’d pack some up for my secret work-boyfriend before I leave.
: You must not like him that much then. Reheated pancakes are the worst. If he was a real threat, he’d be sitting at the table with us right now.
: I’ll take some pancakes, Mom.
: Not until you finish your omelet, you won’t.
: Why did you even ask then?...
: Himawari, are you still able to go to the store with me today? We need to pick up a few things for Geoffrey’s stay.
: And under no circumstance should you forget the hair glue, life vest, or bicycle pump! I promised him that all of these things would be readily available.
: I’ll also need your help remembering the laundry list of absurd items that this man requires for some reason.
: Yeah, I can come. What else do I have going on? I’m a stay-at-home daughter now.
: You sure they're going to be open, though? I thought everything was closed on New Year’s?
: Only one way to find out.
: Works for me. I haven’t set foot outside in three days, though. So I’m going to need you to hold an umbrella over my head to protect me from the sun so I don’t burst into flames.
: We can catch fire together. That way, everyone will know we’re related.
: You’re not in Kumon-mi anymore, Akira. You no longer have to worry about what people will think when they see you with a teenage girl.
: This some sort of PTSD thing from back when you were a cradle-robbing bimbo, Dad?
: Probably. Eat your omelet. Pretend the eggs come from a salmon or something.
: You haven’t touched yours either. You holding out for the pancakes too?
: She’ll cave soon enough. She always does.
: You two are lucky you’re the center of my world, you know. Because at this rate, my secret boyfriend isn’t going to get any and I’ll need to start a new affair when he dumps me.
: Or you could just stay loyal to the man who uprooted his entire life to start over with you in Aomori.
: I don’t know, Dad. It’s really starting to sound like you only relocated to get away from the, like...fifty other Moms who were trying to make babies with you at the same time.
: Yeah, so anyway, that’s a topic we probably shouldn’t bring up at the breakfast table. Or any time during Geoffrey’s stay, for that matter.
: Got it, got it. Extramarital affairs — in. Babies — out. Can we still talk about your harem, though? Was Aunt Sana a part of it?
: I think she still is, Himawari.
: I knew it. I’m gonna give that lady a piece of my mind the next time I need her to buy alcohol for me. Nobody pines after my dad and gets away with it! He’s a married man!
: Mom’s allowed to have as many boyfriends as she wants, though. Pretty sure that’s what womens’ suffrage was all about.
: Yeah, something like that. I’m glad to see your homeschooling is working out.
: Hahah......
: Hah...
: Is that her now? Aunt Sana? Give me the phone. I’ve got some choice words for her about what kinds of men she should go after! I won’t sit idly by as someone tries to tear this family apart!
: Himawari, quiet. I haven’t even started to-
: Is that my niece I hear over there? Good morning, Hima-chan! How are you doing?!
: What’s the matter, Dad? Forget the sound of my voice already?
: Oh, right. Sorry. Forgot I’m not supposed to call you that anymore. Ayane doesn’t like it.
: How about...Sensei, then? For old time’s sake.
: Wow. That shocked, huh? Or are you just banned from talking to me altogether now?
: That’s fine, I guess. Either way, guess who’s in Aomori for the next few nights?
: Want to meet up for dinner or something? Secretly, of course. Wouldn’t want your wife catching wind of you having any sort of tie to the past, after all.
: Oh, and bring Hima-chan along too! It’s been forever since I last saw her. She must be so tall now.
: Akira? Who is it?
: It’s not a debt collector again, is it? I could have sworn I learned from my mistakes and set up autopay on everything after the last time.
: Dad? You’re not going to faint again, are you?
: If you are, try to fall this way. I’m in a better position to catch you than Mom is.
: Akira?...You’re scaring me. I don’t like this.
: Oh, I really don’t like this.
: Um...hello?
: Hima-chan! You remember my voice, don’t you?
: Aunt Ami! Hey! I’m so glad you’re not a debt collector!
: I’m pretty sure you’re not supposed to be calling, though. Mom and Dad both look pretty shook right now.
: I won’t be long. Just wanted to let your father know I’m going to be in Aomori for a few days.
: Really? How come?
: Inspiration, I guess. I try to follow the seasons these days and I’ve heard you guys are in for a few weeks of snow.
: Yeah, it’s really coming down over here. The trains are super delayed. You’re not driving, are you?
: I am. The roads aren’t as bad as you’d expect, though. Have they been plowed near you guys yet?
: Himawari...hang up the phone.
: Sorry, Aunt Ami. I’ve gotta go. It’s nice hearing from you, though. I hope you have fun in Aomori.
: Wait, Hima-chan. Can I talk to your mom first? Just for a second.
: She wants to talk to you. Is that okay?
: Hah...
: Fine. Hand me the phone.
: Hooray! It’s been so long since I last heard my best friend’s voice. I imagine it’s just as beautiful as the last time we-
: There. Problem solved.
: Wow. Not even a trace of hesitation. Stone cold, Mom. Stone cold.
: You guys really fell out hard, didn’t you? You used to be so close. And it still seems like Aunt Ami wants to-
: Our lives are better without her, Himawari. Plus, just look at what her voice did to your father. It’s obvious we’d want no part of that, isn’t it?
: I guess. I still don’t really get it, though. She’s always been so nice to me.
: Good. Because if anyone is ever not nice to you, I will murder them and hang their corpse on our front porch. Ami is no exception to that. Family or not.
: You’re kind of scary when it comes to protecting us, Mom. Like some kind of lion. The blonde just adds to that.
: It almost makes me forget about that time you hit Dad.
: Hima-chan, be a good girl and eat your fucking omelet before Geoffrey-
: Wha- already? He didn’t take the Lamborghini, did he? In this weather?
: Yay! Old person!
: I’ll get it!
: Okay! But don’t let him bring his bags in himself, even if he’s a champion bodybuilder!
: Your father is strong for his age too and he’ll help him once he remembers how to function as a human! You set up the guest room already, right?
: Yup! Water-bed and all! It’ll be like he’s right back at home! I promise!
: How are you feeling? Are you okay? Do you need me to hit you again?
: No...I don’t need to you to hit me.
: I just wish I got some kind of warning beforehand. That way, I could have prepared myself and at least figured out what to say ahead of time.
: I believe that warning comes in the form of one’s name appearing on your phone before answering it- my dear, senile husband.
: Himawari changed all of my contacts to different anime characters last week and I still haven’t figured out who’s who yet.
: Who am I? You talk to me all the time, so I imagine you at least know that.
: Is that really important right now?
: I mean...kind of. Yeah.
: Goku.
: She could have at least given me a girl! What the heck, Hima-chan?!
: Ayane...please. I don’t know what to do.
: Well, what do you want to do? Because it’s not like I’m going to outright ban you from seeing your family. I just...don’t want her influencing our daughter.
: Besides, it’s not like we can avoid her forever. She was always going to come up again and we were always going to have to confront this.
: She sounds more...uhh...stable than I remember.
: Well, I’d sure hope so. She’s had fifteen years to get her shit together. I don’t think she’d last long going around threatening dismemberment as a fully-grown adult.
: And you wouldn’t feel weird if I got dinner with her? Just...to see how she is now?
: Do you want the honest answer or the one I give you to make you feel better?
: Honest. You’re the love of my life and I don’t want to do anything that’ll make you uncomfortable. Especially since-
: The honest answer is that I’m very uncomfortable with it. And that the mere idea of her sinking her claws into you again terrifies me on a level not much does anymore.
: But I trust you. And I trust that you won’t do anything to hurt this family because I know just what it means to you now.
: So if you really want to see her, go ahead.
: Just leave Hima-chan out of it. She doesn’t need to be around-
: Uhh...Mom?
: Hima-chan?
: Could you guys come here for a minute?
The corridor isn’t far from the kitchen.
We can see it from where we are.
That said-
The five seconds it took for me to get there from my seat at the table were the longest of my life.
And the ones that came after were the shortest.
: Uhh...
: Just a...shot in the dark here...but I don’t have a secret evil twin you guys never told me about, right?
: Himawari...
: Go to your room...
: I am so sorry...
: You weren’t supposed to see this...
: Himawari, now.
: Ayane, wait.
: Do you...know what’s going on here, Dad? Because, like...I obviously have a million questions and no clue where to start.
: Akira...you better have a good reason to not be locking her in her room right now.
: Ayane, we wouldn’t be here at all if it weren’t for the...second one. We should at least hear her out, shouldn’t we?
: You know, I’ve always wanted to have a conversation with myself. Which normally just leads to me speaking into the mirror and then feeling weird about it.
: Maybe I could actually try it for real this time? I will call you Himawari Jr.
: Talking won’t change anything...
: I am so...so sorry...
: I suppose you two wouldn’t be willing to trust me a second time, would you?
: Trust you about what? What are you-
: This doesn’t involve you...
: Please...just keep your mouth shut...and I’ll be out of your hair in a minute...
: You’re...
: The one from the roof...right?...
: But how are both of you-
: Because I made a mistake...
: And now you have to hurt even more...
: Hima-chan...whatever this is, we can get through it. You’ve helped us get through it before.
: Please, just raise your head and-
: I don’t deserve to raise my head...
: It will only make this harder...
: Make what harder? What are you-
: I am so...
: So sorry...
: And I know I don’t deserve to ask this of you again, but please...
: Trust me.
: I trust you, Himawari Jr. I’ve always wanted a-
: Oh. Okay.
: Well, you certainly show affection differently than I-
: I feel-
: Things will get better soon...I promise...
: Don’t be scared...
: Just close your eyes...
: WHAT ARE YOU DOING TO HER?! GET AWAY!
: It’s what needs to be done...
: Mistakes stick out too much...
: I am so...sorry...
: HIMA-CHAN! I’M COMING! I-
